prompt:
Revise the immediately preceding dwarf of Moria portrait. Keep the same dwarf identity, square waist-up composition, three-quarter pose, three-part braided beard, mining pick held upright, small belt lantern, clothing silhouette and warm brown drawing on pale cream paper. Simplify the detail moderately, about one third less fine linework. This should sit between basic outline drawing and the existing heavily hatched portrait.
Use clear fine brown contours and medium sparse directional hatching in shadow areas only. Beard and hair should be drawn as larger grouped locks with a few interior strokes, not hundreds of individual hairs. Face should use expressive economical lines, light hatching under brow, beside nose and under cheek, no fine skin texture. Quilted tunic should have a few clean diamond seams, mostly light unshaded paper within each panel. Reduce decorative stitching on shoulder guards to one simple angular border. Mail should be a small suggestion at collar, not detailed rings throughout. Hand anatomy clearly drawn with a few fold lines, no dense texture. Plain pick head with a handful of edge and wear strokes. Lantern with simple outline and a few structural lines. Broader cream highlights across skin and fabric, small deep brown recesses only where forms overlap. Keep visible hand-drawn crosshatching in a few selected shadows so it still has depth and character. Very light ivory paper, less dense background hatching.
Do not change subject, gear, pose or crop. No realistic blended shading, intricate microtexture, photorealism, full color, text, border or watermark. One character only. Square final 640x640 profile.
